title: Match complete command interfaces in GenericSystem mode switches by vpfkfl753 · Pull Request #3596 · ros-controls/ros2_control · GitHub
body_rendered_text:
Description


Related to #3593. GenericSystem still matches joint names by substring, so with calculate_dynamics a switch for joint10/velocity also matches joint1. Prepare rejects it and perform leaves joint10 in position mode. Now both callbacks match the full command interface names. Unsupported modes like effort are still rejected.


Is this user-facing behavior change?


Yes, mock joints with overlapping names (joint1 / joint10) switch modes correctly now.


Did you use Generative AI?


Yes, OpenAI Codex (GPT-6).


Additional Information


The new joint10, prefix_joint1 and controller/joint1 cases fail without the fix. Tested on Rolling (hardware_interface tests + pre-commit).

Pull request overview

This PR fixes mock_components::GenericSystem command-mode switching when joint names overlap (e.g., joint1 vs joint10) by changing mode-switch handling to match exact joint command-interface keys, preventing accidental substring matches and ensuring correct dynamics integration behavior when calculate_dynamics is enabled.


Changes:



Updated GenericSystem::{prepare,perform}_command_mode_switch() to match only fully-qualified joint command interface names declared in the hardware info.


Added regression tests covering overlapping joint-name scenarios (joint10, prefix_joint1, controller/joint1) and validating velocity-mode switching produces the expected position integration.
